question: Two trains of same length are running on parallel tracks in opposite directions with speeds of 54 km/h and 90 km/h respectively. They cross each other in 12 sec. Find the length (in metres) of each train.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (opposite direction) = 54 + 90 = 144 km/h.

Speed in m/s = 144 × (5 ÷ 18) = 40 m/s.

Total distance covered in 12 sec = 40 × 12 = 480 m.

Since both trains have the same length, length of one train = 480 ÷ 2 = 240 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c7b8e1499bcaad78f9d420850a1cf321564ebf396e708d80545a1506db28918.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of first train (S₁) = 54 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 90 km/h

Time taken to cross each other = 12 sec

Let the length of each train be 'L' metres.

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

In opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 54 + 90 = 144 km/h

⇒ Convert km/h to m/s: 144 × (5 ÷ 18) = 40 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Length of Train 1 + Length of Train 2 = L + L = 2L

⇒ 2L = 40 × 12

⇒ 2L = 480

⇒ L = 240

**∴ The correct answer is 240 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Train Crossing Objects

The distance covered when crossing a stationary point (pole or man) is the length of the train itself. When crossing a platform or another train, the total distance is the sum of both lengths.

Speed Conversions

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by (5 ÷ 18). To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by (18 ÷ 5).
